Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses BBQR OF ULTRASONICALLY POWERED BONE CEMENT REMOVAL SYSTE M

1. The system should be an ultrasonically powered surgical system designed sp ecifically for safe and effective removal of PMMA bone cement. 2. The system should operate at a high- frequency ultrasonic resonance of 36 k Hz, ensuring efficient power transmission and enhanced cement softening. 3. The generator should deliver a nominal power output up to 150W with contro lled energy delivery suitable for orthopedic revision procedures. 4. The system should provide displacement amplitude of approximately 100 mi crons, enabling effective cement disruption with minimal applied force. 5. The ultrasonic transducer should be of advanced multi-piezo design, utilizing four piezo-ceramic rings in parallel resonance mode to improve efficiency and r educe heating losses. 6. The transducer design must ensure reduced PZT heating and damage, resulti ng in higher durability and sustained power delivery for large PMMA volumes. 7. The system should operate predominantly in longitudinal vibration mode (≥8 0%) with an additional torsional vibration component (≤20%), enabling dual-mo de energy transmission. 8. The dual vibration mode should provide broader energy dispersion, improved cement heating, and reduced risk of probe stalling within PMMA. 9. The system should feature optimized impedance matching between generato r, transducer probe, and cement to prevent damping of ultrasonic energy by PM MA 10. The probes should be designed to avoid stalling or entrapment within bone cement during operation. 11. The system should be mains-powered, portable and suitable for use in stand ard operating theatre environments. 12. An axial universal ergonomic ultrasonic hand piece should be provided, com patible with a range of cement removal probes and connected to the generator via a robust, medical grade cable. 13. The system should be compatible with single-use sterile and single-use non- sterile (user sterilized) disposable probes and reusable non-sterile (user sterilize d) probes, designed to meet applicable sterilization and clinical performance sta ndards. 14. 1. The system should be an ultrasonically powered surgical system designed sp ecifically for safe and effective removal of PMMA bone cement. 2. The system should operate at a high- frequency ultrasonic resonance of 36 k Hz, ensuring efficient power transmission and enhanced cement softening. 3. The generator should deliver a nominal power output up to 150W with contro lled energy delivery suitable for orthopedic revision procedures. 4. The system should provide displacement amplitude of approximately 100 mi crons, enabling effective cement disruption with minimal applied force. 5. The ultrasonic transducer should be of advanced multi-piezo design, utilizing four piezo-ceramic rings in parallel resonance mode to improve efficiency and r educe heating losses. 6. The transducer design must ensure reduced PZT heating and damage, resulti ng in higher durability and sustained power delivery for large PMMA volumes. 7. The system should operate predominantly in longitudinal vibration mode (≥8 0%) with an additional torsional vibration component (≤20%), enabling dual-mo de energy transmission. 8. The dual vibration mode should provide broader energy dispersion, improved cement heating, and reduced risk of probe stalling within PMMA. 9. The system should feature optimized impedance matching between generato r, transducer probe, and cement to prevent damping of ultrasonic energy by PM MA 10.
